possibilities.connection: OCRia pulls text and layout from pages on one CPU core, so Ling-3.2-air spends its 5.5B active parameters only on reasoning and workflow steps, and Univer gives clerks an agent-editable spreadsheet for the results inside the team's own product.

with.title: Datasette Agent can now create charts on request

possibilities.connection: OCRia turns scanned PDFs into text on a laptop CPU, the rows go into SQLite, and Datasette Agent now builds charts from that data on request.

possibilities.title: Financial planners can read client statements offline at interactive speed on one Mac

with.title: Splash runs Inkling 2 Mini at 200+ tok/s locally

possibilities.connection: On 2026-11-21 Magpie suggested planners read hard statement layouts with Inkling 2 Mini on a laptop when hosted APIs are blocked; today Splash runs Inkling 2 Mini at over 200 tokens per second on an M5 Max and OCRia handles plain pages at about 426 ms each on one CPU core, so the model is only called on hard pages and the session feels live.

appearances.headline: OCRia-nano-1: 8.1M-parameter OCR on one CPU core
appearances.newly_possible: You can run open-weight OCR and layout extraction at about 426 ms per page on a single CPU core.
appearances.why: Document ingestion for RAG and agents no longer needs a GPU or a paid OCR API.
appearances.limits: Speed is LlamaIndex's figure; accuracy against larger OCR models is not shown.
